short: Cross-mode transfer and rank scoring are standard tests; one participant, unstated alignment to vocalized targets and mismatched nulls leave the hierarchy and linear-better claims unsupported.
position: The paper changes two components, both standard: it applies each condition-trained sEEG decoder to the other speech modes (M04), the field's usual transfer test (23 of 33 studies, confirmed, Appendix), and adds sentence-rank scoring to correlation (M12), which an overt-to-covert reconstruction study already ran against a 10,000-shuffle null in seven patients. The hierarchy claim rests on one participant and two repetitions of 100 sentences (Sec. 2.1), and the authors defer its direct test (Sec. 4). The strongest confound is timing: silent trials are scored against vocalized-audio targets (Sec. 2.1) with no stated alignment, where earlier work used dynamic time warping. "Linear better preserves sentence structure" is a slope (Fig. 4), not a level: of six pairs with both AUCs stated, the nonlinear model is higher in three, lower in two, tied in one (Secs. 3.3, 3.4; inference).
